data.description:
## Context
While debugging grindable-deviant-angwantibo, a rival mechanism was falsified for that incident but exposed a separate deterministic liveness gap. tests/conftest.py calls tests/_isolation.py::porcelain during pytest_sessionfinish, after pytest has already printed the per-test `[100%]` progress boundary. `porcelain()` launches `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` with no timeout; the sibling `head()` probe is likewise unbounded.

## Runtime proof
A fake Git that blocked only the second repo-root status call reproduced the exact post-dot boundary. SIGUSR1 captured subprocess.run/_communicate -> tests/_isolation.py:59 porcelain -> tests/conftest.py:681 pytest_sessionfinish. This was not the grindable incident's root cause: 100 natural status probes were median 0.0143s, p95 0.0164s, max 0.0610s, while the incident's observed stack and discriminating A/B identified pytest numbered-temp cleanup.

## Plan
- Define a watchdog-grade local timeout for the read-only repo-isolation Git probes without turning a timeout into a false clean result.
- Exercise the real session-finish lifecycle with a deterministic blocking Git shim and assert a bounded, explicit test-run failure.
- Cover both porcelain() and head() through their real hook/fixture callers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A blocking repo-isolation Git probe cannot keep pytest alive beyond a documented local watchdog.
- [ ] Timeout produces an explicit isolation-infrastructure failure, never `None`/clean success.
- [ ] Real session-finish and per-test commit-guard paths are covered with deterministic subprocess tests.
- [ ] Normal repo-isolation behavior and the default unit suite remain green.
data.title: Repo-isolation session hooks run unbounded Git probes after tests finish
